Asymptomatic mucosal crusting; blood-tinged secretions Symptomatic stenosis or edema/narrowing interfering with airflow; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Stenosis with significant nasal obstruction; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Necrosis of soft tissue or bone; urgent operative intervention indicated Death

records.title: Sinus pain
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the face, between the eyes, or upper teeth originating from the sinuses. Record final diagnosis/cause once determined. Mild pain Moderate pain; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe pain; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Sleep apnea
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by cessation of breathing for short periods during sleep. Snoring and nocturnal sleep arousal without apneic periods Moderate apnea and oxygen desaturation; excessive daytime sleepiness; medical evaluation indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Oxygen desaturation; associated with pulmonary hypertension; medical intervention indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Cardiovascular or neuropsychiatric symptoms; urgent operative intervention indicated Death

records.title: Sneezing
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by the involuntary expulsion of air from the nose. Mild symptoms; intervention not indicated Moderate symptoms; medical intervention indicated

records.title: Sore throat
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by marked discomfort in the throat. Mild pain Moderate pain; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe pain; limiting ability to swallow; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Stridor
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by a high pitched breathing sound due to laryngeal or upper airway obstruction. Respiratory distress; medical intervention indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening airway compromise; urgent intervention indicated (e.g., tracheotomy or intubation) Death

records.title: Tracheal fistula
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by an abnormal communication between the trachea and another organ or anatomic site. Asymptomatic Symptomatic, invasive intervention not indicated Invasive intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Tracheal mucositis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by an inflammation or ulceration involving the mucous membrane of the trachea. Endoscopic findings only; minimal hemoptysis, pain, or respiratory symptoms Moderate symptoms; medical intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe pain; hemorrhage or respiratory symptoms; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Tracheal stenosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by a narrowing of the trachea. Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Symptomatic (e.g., noisy airway breathing), no respiratory distress; medical intervention indicated (e.g., steroids); limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Stridor or respiratory distress; invasive intervention indicated (e.g., stent, laser); limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening airway compromise; urgent intervention indicated (e.g., tracheotomy or intubation) Death

records.title: Voice alteration
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: A disorder characterized by a change in the sound and/or speed of the voice. Mild or intermittent change from normal voice Moderate or persistent change from normal voice; still understandable Severe voice changes including predominantly whispered speech; may require frequent repetition or face-to-face contact for understandability; may require assistive technology

records.title: Respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders - Other, specify
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Respiratory
records.body: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Moderate; minimal, local or noninvasive intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Alopecia
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a decrease in density of hair compared to normal for a given individual at a given age and body location. Hair loss of <50% of normal for that individual that is not obvious from a distance but only on close inspection; a different hair style may be required to cover the hair loss but it does not require a wig or hair piece to camouflage Hair loss of >=50% normal for that individual that is readily apparent to others; a wig or hair piece is necessary if the patient desires to completely camouflage the hair loss; associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Body odor
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an abnormal body smell resulting from the growth of bacteria on the body. Mild odor; physician intervention not indicated; self care interventions Pronounced odor; psychosocial impact; patient seeks medical intervention

records.title: Dermatitis psoriasiform
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by large, red, rounded plaques covered with thicker scales. Present; topical intervention indicated oral intervention indicated IV intervention indicated

records.title: Dermatosis bullous
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by inflammation of the skin characterized by the presence of bullae which are filled with fluid. If infectious, consider Infections and infestations: Rash pustular or other site-specific Infections and infestations term. Asymptomatic Painful blisters; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Blisters covering >50% BSA; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Blisters covering >75% BSA; associated with fluid or electrolyte abnormalities; ICU care or burn unit indicated Death

records.title: Dry skin
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by flaky and dull skin; the pores are generally fine, the texture is a papery thin texture. No associated erythema or pruritus Associated with erythema or pruritus; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Eczematous dermatitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by dry and itchy patches of skin involving the epidermis and superficial dermis and includes some scaling, crusting, or serous oozing. Present; topical intervention indicated Oral intervention indicated IV intervention indicated

records.title: Erythema multiforme
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by target lesions (a pink-red ring around a pale center). Not associated with skin tenderness Associated with skin tenderness Associated with oral or genital erosions Associated with fluid or electrolyte abnormalities; ICU care or burn unit indicated Death

records.title: Erythroderma
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by generalized inflammatory erythema and exfoliation. The inflammatory process involves >90% of the body surface area. Erythema covering >90% BSA without associated symptoms; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Erythema covering >90% BSA with associated symptoms (e.g., pruritus or tenderness); limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Erythema covering >90% BSA with associated fluid or electrolyte abnormalities; ICU care or burn unit indicated Death

records.title: Exfoliative dermatitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by diffuse erythema and scaling involving > 90% of the body surface area. Present; topical intervention indicated oral intervention indicated IV intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Hair color changes
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by change in hair color or loss of normal pigmentation. Present

records.title: Hair texture abnormal
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a change in the way the hair feels. Present

records.title: Hirsutism
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by the presence of excess hair growth in women in anatomic sites where growth is considered to be a secondary male characteristic and under androgen control (beard, moustache, chest, abdomen). In women, increase in length, thickness or density of hair in a male distribution that the patient is able to camouflage by periodic shaving, bleaching, or removal of hair In women, increase in length, thickness or density of hair in a male distribution that requires daily shaving or consistent destructive means of hair removal to camouflage; associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Hyperhidrosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by excessive sweating. Synonym: Night sweats, diaphoresis. Limited to one site (palms, soles, or axillae); self care interventions Involving >1 site; patient seeks medical intervention; associated with psychosocial impact Associated with electrolyte/hemodynamic imbalance

records.title: Hyperkeratosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a thickening of the outer layer of the skin. Present Limiting self-care ADLs or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Hypertrichosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by hair density or length beyond the accepted limits of normal in a particular body region, for a particular age or race. Increase in length, thickness or density of hair that the patient is either able to camouflage by periodic shaving or removal of hairs or is not concerned enough about the overgrowth to use any form of hair removal Increase in length, thickness or density of hair at least on the usual exposed areas of the body [face (not limited to beard/moustache area) plus/minus arms] that requires frequent shaving or use of destructive means of hair removal to camouflage; associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Hypohidrosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by reduced sweating. Symptomatic; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Increase in body temperature; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Lichenoid dermatitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a symmetric eruption of flat-topped, red or purple papules on the trunk and extremities. Present; topical intervention indicated oral intervention indicated IV intervention indicated

records.title: Nail changes
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a change in the nails. Present

records.title: Nail discoloration
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a change in the color of the nail plate. Present

records.title: Nail loss
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by loss of all or a portion of the nail. Asymptomatic separation of the nail bed from the nail plate or nail loss Symptomatic separation of the nail bed from the nail plate or nail loss; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Nail ridging
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by vertical or horizontal ridges on the nails. Present

records.title: Pain of skin
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the skin. Record final diagnosis/cause once determined. Mild pain Moderate pain; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe pain; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by redness, marked discomfort, swelling, and tingling in the palms of the hands or the soles of the feet. Also known as Hand-Foot Syndrome. Minimal skin changes or dermatitis (e.g., erythema, edema, or hyperkeratosis) without pain Skin changes (e.g., peeling, blisters, bleeding, fissures, edema, or hyperkeratosis) with pain; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe skin changes (e.g., peeling, blisters, bleeding, fissures, edema, or hyperkeratosis) with pain; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Papulovesicular rash
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an eruption consisting of papules (a small, raised pimple) and vesicles (a small fluid filled blister). Asymptomatic Associated with psychosocial impact; mild symptoms Covering >50% BSA; moderate or severe symptoms Blisters covering >75% BSA; life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Photosensitivity
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an increase in sensitivity of the skin to light. Painless erythema Tender erythema Erythema with blistering; oral corticosteroid therapy indicated; pain control indicated (e.g., narcotics or NSAIDs) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Pruritus
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an intense itching sensation. Mild or localized; topical intervention indicated Widespread and intermittent; skin changes from scratching (e.g., edema, papulation, excoriations, lichenification, oozing/crusts); oral intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Widespread and constant; systemic corticosteroid or immunosuppressive therapy indicated; limiting sleep or self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Purpura
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by hemorrhagic areas of the skin and mucous membrane. Newer lesions appear reddish in color. Older lesions are usually a darker purple color and eventually become a brownish-yellow color. Combined area of lesions covering <10% BSA Combined area of lesions covering 10 - 30% BSA Combined area of lesions covering >30% BSA

records.title: Pustular drug eruption
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by the development of nonfollicular, sterile pustules on an erythematous base. Asymptomatic Associated with psychosocial impact; oral antibiotics or steroid indicated; local intervention indicated (e.g., topical antibiotic, antifungal, or antiviral); limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe symptoms; IV antibiotic or steroid indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Rash maculo-papular
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by the presence of macules (flat) and papules (elevated). Also known as morbilliform rash, it is one of the most common cutaneous adverse events, frequently affecting the upper trunk, spreading centripetally and associated with pruritis. Consider Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders: Pustular drug eruption. Asymptomatic Mild symptoms Macules/papules covering >50% BSA; moderate or severe symptoms Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Scalp pain
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a sensation of marked discomfort in the skin covering the top and the back of the head. Record final diagnosis/cause once determined. Mild pain Moderate pain; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe pain; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Skin atrophy
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by the degeneration and thinning of the epidermis and dermis. Associated with telangiectasias or changes in skin color Associated with striae or adnexal structure loss Associated with ulceration

records.title: Skin hyperpigmentation
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by darkening of the skin due to excessive melanin deposition. Present Associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Skin hypopigmentation
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by loss of skin pigment (e.g., vitiligo). Present Associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Skin induration
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an area of hardness in the skin. Mild induration, able to move skin parallel to plane (sliding) and perpendicular to skin (pinching up) Moderate induration, able to slide skin, unable to pinch skin; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe induration; unable to slide or pinch skin; limiting joint or orifice movement (e.g., mouth, anus); limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Generalized; associated with signs or symptoms of impaired breathing or feeding Death

records.title: Skin ulceration
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by a circumscribed, erosive lesion on the skin. Combined area of ulcers <1 cm; nonblanchable erythema of intact skin with associated warmth or edema Combined area of ulcers 1 - 2 cm; partial thickness skin loss involving skin or subcutaneous fat Combined area of ulcers >2 cm; full-thickness skin loss involving damage to or necrosis of subcutaneous tissue that may extend down to fascia Any size ulcer with extensive destruction, tissue necrosis, or damage to muscle, bone, or supporting structures with or without full thickness skin loss Death

records.title: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by less than 10% total body skin area separation of dermis. The syndrome is thought to be a hypersensitivity complex affecting the skin and the mucous membranes. Skin sloughing covering <10% BSA Skin sloughing covering >=10% BSA; life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Subcutaneous emphysema
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by air in the subcutaneous tissue. Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Moderate; minimal, local or noninvasive intervention indicated Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Telangiectasia
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by local dilatation of small vessels resulting in red discoloration of the skin or mucous membranes. Present Associated with psychosocial impact

records.title: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by greater than 30% total body skin area separation of dermis. The syndrome is thought to be a hypersensitivity complex affecting the skin and the mucous membranes. Skin sloughing covering >=30% BSA with associated symptoms (e.g., erythema, purpura, or epidermal detachment); life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Urticaria
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: A disorder characterized by an itchy skin eruption characterized by wheals with pale interiors and well-defined red margins. Consider Immune system disorders: Allergic reaction, Anaphylaxis. Topical intervention indicated Oral intervention indicated IV intervention indicated

records.title: Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders - Other, specify
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Skin / subcutaneous
records.body: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Moderate; minimal, local or noninvasive intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Arterial thromboembolism
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by occlusion of an arterial vessel by a blood clot that develops in an artery. Consider Nervous system disorders: Stroke, Transient ischemic attacks for CNS-related events or Cardiac disorders: Myocardial infarction. Urgent intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences; hemodynamic or neurologic instability; organ damage; loss of extremity(ies) Death

records.title: Capillary leak syndrome
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by leakage of intravascular fluids into the extravascular space. This syndrome is observed in patients who demonstrate a state of generalized leaky capillaries following shock syndromes, low-flow states, ischemia-reperfusion injuries, toxemias, medications, or poisoning. It can lead to generalized edema and multiple organ failure. Asymptomatic Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated Severe symptoms Life-threatening consequences Death

records.title: Cyanosis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a bluish discoloration of the skin and/or mucous membranes. Present

records.title: Flushing
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by episodic reddening of the skin, especially face, neck, or chest. Mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only Moderate symptoms; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Symptomatic, associated with hypotension and/or tachycardia; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Hematoma
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel. Report subdural and epidural hematoma under Nervous system disorders: Intracranial hemorrhage. Mild symptoms; intervention not indicated Minimally invasive evacuation or aspiration indicated Transfusion; invasive intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Hot flashes
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by an uncomfortable and temporary sensation of intense body warmth, flushing, sometimes accompanied by sweating upon cooling. Mild symptoms; intervention not indicated Moderate symptoms; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe symptoms; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Hypertension
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a pathological increase in blood pressure. Adult: Systolic BP 140 - 159 mmHg or diastolic BP 90 - 99 mmHg; recurrent or persistent; Pediatric and adolescent: Recurrent or persistent (>=24 hrs) BP >ULN; monotherapy indicated; systolic and /or diastolic BP between the 95th percentile and 5 mmHg above the 99th percentile; Adolescent: Systolic between 130 - 139 or diastolic between 80 - 89 even if <95th percentile Adult: Systolic BP 160 - 179 mmHg or diastolic BP 100 - 109 mmHg persisting over 1 hour; SBP >140 and plus either increase in SBP >20 mmHg or increase MAP >15 mmHg from baseline; Pediatric and adolescent: Systolic and/or diastolic >5 mmHg above the 99 th percentile Adult and Pediatric: SBP≥180 or DBP ≥110 mmHg persisting over 1 hour; BP associated with acute hypertension mediated organ damage; life-threatening consequences (e.g., malignant hypertension, transient or permanent neurologic deficit, hypertensive crisis); urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Hypotension
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a blood pressure that is below the normal expected for an individual in a given environment. Asymptomatic, intervention not indicated Non-urgent medical intervention indicated Medical intervention indicated; hospitalization indicated Life-threatening consequences and urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Lymph leakage
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by the loss of lymph fluid into the surrounding tissue or body cavity. Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated Severe symptoms; invasive intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Lymphedema
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by excessive fluid collection in tissues that causes swelling. Record final diagnosis/cause once determined. Trace thickening or faint discoloration Marked discoloration; leathery skin texture; papillary formation; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe symptoms; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric)

records.title: Lymphocele
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a cystic lesion containing lymph. Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated Severe symptoms; invasive intervention indicated

records.title: Peripheral ischemia
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by impaired circulation to an extremity. Brief (<24 hrs) episode of ischemia managed medically and without permanent deficit; claudication Prolonged (>=24 hrs) or recurring symptoms and/or invasive intervention indicated; pain at rest Life-threatening consequences; major tissue loss; urgent operative intervention indicated Death

records.title: Phlebitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by inflammation of the wall of a peripheral vein associated with an intravenous line. Present

records.title: Superficial thrombophlebitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by a blood clot and inflammation involving a superficial vein of the extremities. Present

records.title: Superior vena cava syndrome
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by obstruction of the blood flow in the superior vena cava. Signs and symptoms include swelling and cyanosis of the face, neck, and upper arms, cough, orthopnea and headache. Asymptomatic; incidental finding of SVC thrombosis Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated (e.g., anticoagulation, radiation or chemotherapy) Severe symptoms; multi-modality intervention indicated (e.g., anticoagulation, chemotherapy, radiation, stenting) Life-threatening consequences; urgent multi-modality intervention indicated (e.g., lysis, thrombectomy, surgery) Death

records.title: Vasculitis
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by inflammation involving the wall of a vessel. Asymptomatic, intervention not indicated Moderate symptoms, medical intervention indicated Severe symptoms, medical intervention indicated (e.g., steroids) Life-threatening consequences; evidence of peripheral or visceral ischemia; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Venous thromboembolism
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: A disorder characterized by occlusion of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream (for example, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), etc.). Consider Nervous system disorders: Stroke, Transient ischemic attacks for CNS-related events. Use Vascular disorders: Arterial thromboembolism for arterial thrombi. Use Injury, poisoning and procedural complications: Vascular access complication if related to a catheter. Medical intervention not indicated (e.g., superficial thrombosis) Medical intervention indicated Urgent medical intervention indicated Life-threatening consequences with hemodynamic or neurologic instability Death

records.title: Vascular disorders - Other, specify
records.subtitle: CTCAE grading · Vascular
records.body: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated Moderate; minimal, local or noninvasive intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL or mild/moderate impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization indicated; limiting self-care ADL or severe impact on age-appropriate normal daily activity (pediatric) Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated Death

records.title: Bullous dermatoses
records.subtitle: irAE management · Dermatologic
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 pd1 pdl1 Dermatosis bullous s20-dermatosis-bullous Exclude Other cause of blistering - infection, another drug, or systemic disease. Confirm autoimmune bullous disease (most commonly bullous pemphigoid) with skin biopsy + direct immunofluorescence and serology (BP antibodies, desmoglein 1/3, indirect IF). Watch for DIHS/DRESS features. Baseline Full skin + mucous-membrane exam; ROS for skin pain, fever, and mucosal/ocular/genital involvement. Urgent dermatology for biopsy (perilesional, one specimen for DIF) + serologic workup. Red flags Mucous-membrane involvement, increasing BSA, or skin sloughing -> admit / burn unit; monitor for progression to SCAR (SJS/TEN). rf Rechallenge Bullous disease generally needs temporary or permanent discontinuation. G4 -> permanently discontinue; NCCN discontinues from G3. Lower grades: hold, resume only per dermatology once resolved. rc G1 c1 Asymptomatic; blisters <10% BSA, no associated erythema ICI Continue if asymptomatic, non-inflammatory blisters (eg friction/pressure); NCCN: consider holding. Any symptomatic bullae or erosions = treat as >=G2 Topical Local wound care; high-potency topical corticosteroid (NCCN) ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.2 Bullous Dermatoses), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3 G2 c2 Blisters 10%-30% BSA; painful blisters; limiting iADL ICI Hold (NCCN: until <G1); consult dermatology for steroid-sparing options + resuming Steroids Low threshold for prednisone (or equivalent) 0.5-1 mg/kg/day, taper >=4 wk (NCCN: taper 4-6 wk) Topical Class 1 high-potency topical steroid (clobetasol, betamethasone), reassess every 3 days; petrolatum wound care Escalation If bullous pemphigoid confirmed (biopsy/serology): consider rituximab or dupilumab (NCCN); if no improvement after 3 days -> urgent dermatology Referral Dermatology ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.2 Bullous Dermatoses), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3 G3 c3 Skin sloughing / blisters >30% BSA with pain; limiting self-care ADL ICI Hold and consider admission (NCCN: discontinue from G3) Steroids IV methylprednisolone (or equivalent) 1-2 mg/kg, convert to oral when appropriate, taper >=4 wk Escalation If bullous pemphigoid: steroid-sparing options - IVIG, rituximab (NCCN: dupilumab recommended; IVIG as adjunct to rituximab) Referral Urgent dermatology; inpatient ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.2 Bullous Dermatoses), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3 G4 c4 Blisters >30% BSA with fluid/electrolyte abnormalities; ICU/burn unit indicated ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids IV methylprednisolone (or equivalent) 1-2 mg/kg, convert to oral when appropriate, taper >=4 wk Escalation Steroid-sparing options if bullous pemphigoid - IVIG (2 g/kg over 2-5 days), rituximab, dupilumab Referral Admit immediately under a dermatologist; inpatient care required ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.2 Bullous Dermatoses), G4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3

records.title: Inflammatory dermatitis / maculopapular rash
records.subtitle: irAE management · Dermatologic
records.body: CTLA-4 · combo > PD-1/PD-L1 ctla4 pd1 pdl1 combo Rash maculo-papular s20-rash-maculo-papular Papulovesicular rash s20-papulovesicular-rash Eczematous dermatitis s20-eczematous-dermatitis Lichenoid dermatitis s20-lichenoid-dermatitis Exclude Other drug (photosensitisers; DRESS-risk drugs - antiepileptics, allopurinol, sulfonamides, vancomycin), infection, or skin disease from another systemic/primary disorder. Review the full medication list. DRESS clues: facial/hand oedema, eosinophilia, LFT rise. Baseline History + full skin exam incl. oral mucosa; document BSA involved and any blister formation. CBC (eosinophil count), CMP/LFTs, peripheral smear if DRESS suspected. Consider skin biopsy and serial clinical photography. Red flags Blistering, mucosal involvement, skin pain, >30% BSA, or systemic features -> monitor for progression to SCAR (SJS/TEN); G4 -> admit. rf Rechallenge G1-2 continue/hold; after G3 resume once <=G1 and prednisone <10 mg/day with close monitoring. G4: prefer alternative antineoplastic; restart only if resolved to G1 and ICPi is the sole option. rc G1 c1 Rash <10% BSA, +/- pruritus or tenderness ICI Continue Topical Mild-moderate potency topical corticosteroid + emollients (NCCN: moderate potency); avoid skin irritants Supportive Oral antihistamine for pruritus if present ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-1 G2 c2 10%-30% BSA +/- symptoms, limiting iADL; or >30% BSA with mild symptoms ICI Consider holding; monitor weekly. If not improved after 4 wk, regrade as G3 (NCCN: may continue) Topical Medium-to-high potency topical corticosteroid + emollients; oral antihistamines Steroids Consider prednisone (or equivalent) 0.5-1 mg/kg, taper over 4 wk (NCCN: prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day only if unresponsive to topical within 1-2 wk) Referral Consider dermatology ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-1 G3 c3 >30% BSA with moderate/severe symptoms; limiting self-care ADL ICI Hold; consult dermatology re appropriateness of resuming Topical High-potency topical corticosteroid + emollients + oral antihistamines; phototherapy for severe pruritus Steroids Oral prednisone (or equivalent) 1 mg/kg/day, taper over >=4 wk (NCCN: prednisone/IV methylprednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day, taper 4-6 wk) Work-up + Consider skin biopsy; consider inpatient care (NCCN) Referral Urgent dermatology ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-1 G4 c4 Severe consequences needing hospitalisation / urgent intervention; life-threatening ICI Immediate hold; permanent discontinuation likely if unresolved Steroids IV methylprednisolone (or equivalent) 1-2 mg/kg, slow taper once toxicity resolves Escalation Monitor closely for progression to SCAR Work-up + Admit with direct oncology involvement Referral Urgent dermatology ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis), G4

records.title: Pruritus
records.subtitle: irAE management · Dermatologic
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · CTLA-4 pd1 pdl1 ctla4 Pruritus s20-pruritus Exclude Other causes of pruritus - cholestasis (bile acids), renal (BUN/creatinine), thyroid dysfunction, and evolving bullous pemphigoid (check BP antibodies). Distinguish pruritus with vs without rash. Baseline Total body skin exam incl. mucosa; assess history of prior inflammatory dermatologic disease. If atypical/refractory: bullous pemphigoid antibodies, BUN/creatinine, LFTs, TFTs, bile acids; serum IgE + histamine at G3 (NCCN). Red flags Intense, widespread, constant itch limiting sleep/self-care, or new blistering -> hold ICPi, systemic steroids, urgent dermatology. rf Rechallenge G1 continue; G2-3 hold and resume once improved to <=G1. rc G1 c1 Mild or localised ICI Continue Topical Moderate-potency topical corticosteroid for localised pruritus; OTC anti-itch cream (pramoxine, menthol, camphor, hydrocortisone 0.5-1%) Supportive Oral antihistamines; whole-body non-fragranced moisturiser ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis: pruritus), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-2 G2 c2 Intense/widespread, intermittent; scratching-related skin changes; limiting iADL ICI NCCN: hold. ASCO (pruritus without rash): may continue with symptomatic control Steroids NCCN: prednisone/IV methylprednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day (G2-3 block), taper 4-6 wk Antipruritic Gabapentinoids (gabapentin, pregabalin); ASCO adds refrigerated menthol / pramoxine topically; oral antihistamines Referral Urgent dermatology (NCCN) ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis: pruritus), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-2 G3 c3 Intense/widespread, constant; limiting self-care ADL or sleep ICI Hold Steroids Prednisone/IV methylprednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day, taper 4-6 wk (NCCN) Antipruritic Gabapentinoids; if no response in 1 month -> dupilumab, omalizumab, or narrow-band UVB (NCCN). ASCO: gabapentin, pregabalin, aprepitant, or dupilumab Work-up + Serum IgE + histamine (omalizumab if IgE high; antihistamines if histamine high) Referral Urgent dermatology ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.1 Rash/Inflammatory Dermatitis: pruritus), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-2

records.title: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS / TEN)
records.subtitle: irAE management · Dermatologic
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · CTLA-4 · combo pd1 pdl1 ctla4 combo Stevens-Johnson syndrome s20-stevens-johnson-syndrome Toxic epidermal necrolysis s20-toxic-epidermal-necrolysis Erythema multiforme s20-erythema-multiforme Exclude Another culprit drug (evaluate the full medication list - antibiotics, anticonvulsants), infection, or other systemic disease. Skin biopsy to confirm full-thickness epidermal necrosis (SJS/TEN) and exclude AGEP, paraneoplastic pemphigus, other autoimmune blistering. Baseline Total-body skin exam incl. ALL mucous membranes + complete ROS. CBC with differential, LFTs, renal function; UA (DRESS-associated nephritis); blood cultures if febrile. Skin biopsy; serial clinical photography. Red flags Dermatologic emergency. Mucosal involvement, skin pain, epidermal detachment, systemic symptoms, or LFT elevation (DRESS/DIHS) -> burn unit / ICU. Even limited BSA bullae/erosions may progress to G3-4. rf Rechallenge Do NOT rechallenge - suspected SJS/TEN or any mucous-membrane involvement (not isolated stomatitis) mandates ICPi discontinuation; permanent at G4. rc G3 c3 Skin sloughing <10% BSA (SJS) with mucosal-involvement signs (erythema, purpura, epidermal/mucous-membrane detachment) ICI Discontinue (suspected SJS / any mucosal involvement). ASCO: hold + consult dermatology pending confirmation Steroids IV methylprednisolone (or equivalent) 0.5-1 mg/kg, convert to oral on response, wean >=4 wk (NCCN: 1-2 mg/kg/day). Steroids are NOT contraindicated here - T-cell-mediated mechanism Escalation Immunosuppression warranted (ASCO Table A2); NCCN: consider IVIG (2 g/kg over 2-5 days), etanercept, or cyclosporine Supportive Burn unit / wound care - fluid + electrolyte balance, minimise insensible losses, prevent infection; topical emollients + high-strength topical steroid Referral Urgent dermatology; ophthalmology / ENT / urology / gynaecology for mucosal involvement ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.3 SCAR), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3 G4 c4 Detachment >=10% BSA (TEN) with signs +/- systemic symptoms and abnormal bloods (eg LFT rise in DRESS/DIHS) ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids IV methylprednisolone (or equivalent) 1-2 mg/kg, tapering when toxicity resolves to normal Escalation IVIG or cyclosporine in severe / steroid-unresponsive cases (NCCN: also etanercept) Supportive Admit to burn unit or ICU; pain / palliative consultation and admission for DRESS manifestations Referral Dermatology + wound care; ophthalmology / urology / gynaecology / ENT for mucosal surfaces ASCO 2021 · Table 1 (1.3 SCAR), G4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_DERM-3

records.title: Colitis / immune-mediated diarrhoea
records.subtitle: irAE management · Gastrointestinal
records.body: CTLA-4 · combo > PD-1/L1 ctla4 combo pd1 pdl1 Diarrhea s5-diarrhea Colitis s5-colitis Enterocolitis s5-enterocolitis Exclude Infection (C. diff, CMV) & other diarrhoea causes; NSAIDs may worsen. Send stool markers before immunosuppression. Baseline CBC, CMP, TSH; stool culture / C. diff / O&P / CMV; fecal lactoferrin + calprotectin. Red flags Blood/mucus, fever, abdominal distension -> escalate/admit; watch perforation, typhlitis. rf Rechallenge PD-1/PD-L1 may restart once resolved to <=G1 & prednisone <=10 mg/day; do not restart the CTLA-4 agent. rc G1 c1 <4 stools/day over baseline ICI Continue (may hold briefly, resume if <=G1) Steroids Not routinely indicated Supportive Hydration, diet; loperamide only after infection excluded ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.1 Colitis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-2 G2 c2 4-6 stools/day over baseline ICI Hold. Grade >=2: consider permanently discontinuing CTLA-4 (may restart PD-1/PD-L1) Steroids Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day (NCCN 1-2; budesonide 9 mg/day option), taper 4-6 wk once <=G1 Escalation No response ~3 days -> infliximab 5 mg/kg or vedolizumab (wk 0/2/6) Work-up + Colonoscopy/biopsy if markers or symptoms; CT A/P if complications suspected Referral Gastroenterology ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.1 Colitis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-3 G3 c3 >=7 stools/day; hospitalisation indicated ICI Hold; consider permanently discontinuing CTLA-4 (discontinue current regimen if on combination) Steroids Prednisone / IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day until <=G1, taper 4-6 wk Escalation Refractory 3-5 days -> infliximab 5 mg/kg (wk 0/2/6) -> vedolizumab 300 mg (NCCN: tofacitinib/ustekinumab if biologic-refractory) Work-up + Endoscopy + biopsy; consider admission Referral Gastroenterology ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.1 Colitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-4 G4 c4 life-threatening consequences ICI Permanently discontinue ICI (all agents) Steroids IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day, start immediately; taper 4-6 wk once <=G1 Escalation Early infliximab 5 mg/kg if refractory; vedolizumab 300 mg Work-up + Admit; exclude perforation / toxic megacolon; surgical review if needed Referral Gastroenterology + inpatient (+/- surgery) ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.1 Colitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-4

records.title: Hepatitis (immune-mediated)
records.subtitle: irAE management · Hepatic
records.body: CTLA-4 · combo > PD-1/PD-L1 ctla4 combo pd1 pdl1 Alanine aminotransferase increased s11-alanine-aminotransferase-increased True Aspartate aminotransferase increased s11-aspartate-aminotransferase-increased True Blood bilirubin increased s11-blood-bilirubin-increased True Hepatitis s7-hepatitis Exclude Viral hepatitis (A/B/C), alcohol, and other drug-induced liver injury (review meds/supplements, acetaminophen); disease-related hepatic dysfunction / liver metastases or progression. For isolated transaminase rise check CK/aldolase (myositis, rhabdomyolysis) and ferritin (HLH). If autoimmune hepatitis suspected: ANA / ASMA / ANCA. Baseline AST, ALT, and bilirubin (total + direct), ALKP, albumin before each infusion; weekly if G1 elevation. For grade >=2 add viral serologies, iron studies, autoimmune panel, GGT if ALKP-predominant, PT/INR, and abdominal imaging (ultrasound / contrast CT or MRI). Red flags Concomitant bilirubin >2 mg/dL raises risk of hepatic failure (unless Gilbert); synthetic dysfunction (rising INR, ascites, encephalopathy) or AST/ALT >8x ULN -> inpatient care. rf Rechallenge G2: resume once recovered to <=G1 and prednisone <=10 mg/day. G3: consider permanent discontinuation if asymptomatic, permanently discontinue if symptomatic. G4: permanently discontinue. rc G1 c1 AST or ALT >ULN to 3x ULN and/or total bilirubin >ULN to 1.5x ULN (NCCN <3x ULN); asymptomatic ICI Continue with close monitoring (NCCN: consider holding for a concerning lab-value trend); consider alternate etiologies Steroids Not indicated - no treatment for G1 LFT abnormality Work-up + Monitor LFTs 1-2x weekly ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.2 Hepatitis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-5 G2 c2 AST or ALT >3 to 5x ULN and/or total bilirubin >1.5 to 3x ULN; asymptomatic ICI Hold temporarily; also hold other potentially hepatotoxic oncologic drugs and stop unnecessary hepatotoxic medications Steroids Prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day if no improvement after 3-5 days (NCCN 3-7 days; max 60 mg/day). Taper over at least 1 month once <=G1; resume ICPi when steroid <=10 mg/day Escalation If inadequate improvement after 3 days, add mycophenolate mofetil (NCCN: MMF up to 1.5 g q12h, or tacrolimus). Infliximab is CONTRAINDICATED in immune-mediated hepatitis Work-up + Increase LFT monitoring to every 3 days (NCCN 3-5 days) + PT/INR; workup other causes (viral, iron studies, autoimmune panel, imaging) Referral Hepatology consult for G2 and above ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.2 Hepatitis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-5 G3 c3 AST or ALT 5-20x ULN and/or total bilirubin 3-10x ULN, OR symptomatic liver dysfunction; fibrosis by biopsy; compensated cirrhosis; chronic hepatitis reactivation ICI Consider permanently discontinuing if asymptomatic; permanently discontinue if symptomatic (NCCN: hold) Steroids Immediately start methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day (NCCN: prednisone / IV methylprednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day). Taper ~4-6 wk once <=G1, re-escalate if needed Escalation If steroid-refractory add azathioprine (test TPMT) or mycophenolate mofetil once infection excluded (NCCN: MMF or tacrolimus if no improvement 1-2 days; refractory -> tocilizumab / other steroid-sparing). Infliximab CONTRAINDICATED (hepatotoxic) Work-up + Labs daily / every other day; inpatient monitoring if AST/ALT >8x ULN or bilirubin >3x ULN; consider liver biopsy if steroid-refractory or atypical/cholestatic Referral Urgent GI / hepatology referral if no improvement after 7 days; consider tertiary transfer ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.2 Hepatitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-6 G4 c4 AST or ALT >20x ULN and/or total bilirubin >10x ULN, OR decompensated liver function (ascites, coagulopathy, encephalopathy, coma) ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids Methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day (NCCN: prednisone / IV methylprednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day with early concomitant MMF; may start steroids while awaiting results) Escalation Add mycophenolate mofetil / tacrolimus if no improvement after 1-2 days; tocilizumab or other steroid-sparing if refractory. Infliximab CONTRAINDICATED Work-up + Inpatient care; LFTs every 1-3 days; PT/INR; consider diagnostic liver biopsy Referral GI / hepatology ASCO 2021 · Table 2 (2.2 Hepatitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_GI-6

records.title: Pneumonitis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Pulmonary
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo > CTLA-4 pd1 pdl1 combo ctla4 Pneumonitis s19-pneumonitis Exclude Infection - viral (influenza, COVID-19, RSV), bacterial, fungal, AFB, PJP; pulmonary embolus; lymphangitic tumour spread / malignant lung infiltration; cardiac causes. Assume the patient may be immunocompromised. Baseline History and physical, pulse oximetry (resting + ambulation); chest CT preferably with contrast (rule out PE / other etiologies). For grade >=2: infectious workup - nasal swab, sputum culture, blood culture, urine antigen (pneumococcus, legionella). Red flags New oxygen requirement / hypoxia, involvement of all lobes or >50% of parenchyma, or respiratory compromise -> admit. Steroid-refractory if no clinical improvement after 48-72 h of steroids. rf Rechallenge G1: may resume once radiographic improvement or resolution (if no improvement, treat as G2). G2: hold until <=G1. G3-4: permanently discontinue. rc G1 c1 Asymptomatic; confined to one lobe or <25% of lung parenchyma; clinical/diagnostic observations only ICI Hold, or proceed with close monitoring (NCCN: consider holding); may resume with radiographic improvement/resolution - if none, treat as G2 Steroids Not routinely indicated Work-up + Monitor weekly (H&P, pulse oximetry); repeat chest imaging in 3-4 wk (NCCN 4-6 wk) or sooner if symptomatic; consider repeat spirometry / DLCO in 3-4 wk if baseline available ASCO 2021 · Table 3 (3.1 Pneumonitis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_PULM-1 G2 c2 Symptomatic; involves >1 lobe or 25-50% of parenchyma; medical intervention indicated; limiting instrumental ADL ICI Hold until clinical improvement to <=G1 Steroids Prednisone / methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day; taper over 4-6 wk once <=G1 Escalation If no clinical improvement after 48-72 h of steroids, treat as G3. NCCN: mycophenolate mofetil as steroid-sparing agent for steroid-dependent pneumonitis at taper Work-up + Monitor >=weekly (H&P, pulse oximetry, +/- imaging); consider bronchoscopy with BAL +/- transbronchial biopsy; empiric antibiotics if infection remains in differential Referral Pulmonary + infectious disease consults ASCO 2021 · Table 3 (3.1 Pneumonitis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_PULM-1 G3 c3 Severe symptoms; hospitalization required; involves all lobes or >50% of parenchyma; limiting self-care ADL; oxygen indicated ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids Methylprednisolone IV 1-2 mg/kg/day; assess response within 48 h; taper over 4-6 wk (NCCN >=6 wk) Escalation If no improvement after 48 h add second-line: infliximab, mycophenolate mofetil IV (NCCN 1-1.5 g BID), IVIG (2 g/kg over 2-5 days), or cyclophosphamide (NCCN preferred: IVIG or tocilizumab) Work-up + Inpatient care; infectious workup; bronchoscopy with BAL +/- transbronchial biopsy if tolerated; empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (incl. atypicals) if infection not excluded Referral Pulmonary + infectious disease consults ASCO 2021 · Table 3 (3.1 Pneumonitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_PULM-2 G4 c4 Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention indicated (intubation) ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day; assess response within 48 h; taper over >=6 wk Escalation Add second-line if no improvement after 48 h - NCCN preferred IVIG or tocilizumab; also mycophenolate mofetil or infliximab 5 mg/kg (may repeat at 14 days) Work-up + Inpatient / ICU care; infectious workup incl. immunocompromised panel; bronchoscopy with BAL if feasible; empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics Referral Pulmonary + infectious disease consults ASCO 2021 · Table 3 (3.1 Pneumonitis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_PULM-2

records.title: Hypophysitis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Endocrine
records.body: CTLA-4 · combo > PD-1 ctla4 combo pd1 Hypophysitis s3-hypophysitis Hypopituitarism s3-hypopituitarism Exclude Pituitary metastasis / other sellar lesion (MRI if DI or mass symptoms). Baseline AM ACTH + cortisol, TSH, FT4, electrolytes (Na); ACTH stimulation if indeterminate; MRI brain with pituitary cuts, especially for diabetes insipidus / mass symptoms. Red flags Adrenal crisis — start corticosteroid FIRST when multiple deficiencies (other hormones accelerate cortisol clearance → crisis). rf Rechallenge Hold during acute phase; ICI may resume once stabilised on replacement (endocrinopathy exception). rc G1 c1 Asymptomatic / mild ICI Hold until stabilised on replacement, then resume (endocrinopathy exception) Replacement Hydrocortisone 15–20 mg/day divided for secondary AI; add thyroid replacement (goal FT4 upper-half range) AFTER adrenal replacement; other axes as needed ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.3), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-3 G2 c2 Moderate symptoms, ADL intact ICI Hold until stabilised on replacement Replacement As G1 (adrenal first, then thyroid/other) Steroids Pulse prednisone 1 mg/kg/day if MRI swelling / optic chiasm threat; taper 1–2 wk to physiologic (≤5 mg) Referral Endocrinology ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.3), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-3 G3 c3 Severe symptoms; medically significant ICI Hold Steroids IV stress-dose hydrocortisone 50–100 mg Q6–8h; oral pulse prednisone 1–2 mg/kg/day, taper ≥1–2 wk to physiologic Replacement Maintenance as G1 ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.3), G3–4 G4 c4 Life-threatening ICI Hold; admit Steroids IV stress-dose hydrocortisone; taper over 5–7 days to oral maintenance Replacement Maintenance as G1 ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.3), G3–4

records.title: Hypothyroidism
records.subtitle: irAE management · Endocrine
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Hypothyroidism s3-hypothyroidism Exclude Central hypothyroidism (low TSH + low FT4 → evaluate as hypophysitis); non-thyroidal illness. Often follows a thyrotoxic/thyroiditis phase. Baseline TSH (± FT4) every 4–6 wk on ICI; TSH + FT4 for case detection in symptomatic patients. Red flags Severe/myxoedema (rare) → inpatient. If primary vs central uncertain, give hydrocortisone before levothyroxine. rf Rechallenge Endocrinopathy exception — ICI usually continued; permanent discontinuation not required. Hold only for severe, resume once euthyroid on replacement. rc G1 c1 TSH >4.5–<10 mIU/L, asymptomatic ICI Continue, with TSH (± FT4) monitoring every 4–6 wk Replacement None routinely; levothyroxine only if TSH persists >10 (measured 4 wk apart) ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.1), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-2 G2 c2 Moderate symptoms, ADL intact; TSH persistently >10 ICI May continue or hold until symptoms resolve to baseline Replacement Levothyroxine — symptomatic (any TSH elevation) or asymptomatic TSH >10; titrate to TSH in range, monitor every 6–8 wk Referral Endocrinology for atypical or suspected central hypothyroidism ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.1), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-2 G3 c3 Severe symptoms; medically significant ICI Hold until symptoms resolve to baseline on replacement Replacement Levothyroxine; endocrine consult Work-up + Consider inpatient assessment ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.1), G3–4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-2 G4 c4 Life-threatening (myxoedema coma) ICI Hold Replacement Inpatient endocrinology — IV levothyroxine, steroids, supportive care Acute Admit ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.1), G3–4

records.title: Insulin-dependent diabetes (T1DM / DKA)
records.subtitle: irAE management · Endocrine
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Diabetes mellitus s12-diabetes-mellitus Hyperglycemia s12-hyperglycemia True Exclude T2DM / steroid-induced hyperglycaemia. Check anti-GAD / islet-cell Ab, C-peptide, insulin — but do not delay insulin. Baseline Glucose; screen for DKA (ketones, pH, anion gap); antibodies + C-peptide (confirm ICI-T1DM once euglycaemic). See the Hyperglycemia calculator. Red flags DKA — life-threatening if insulin withheld; urgent/emergent evaluation; admit. rf Rechallenge Insulin is lifelong (beta-cell destruction). ICI often continued (mild) or held until glucose controlled — endocrinopathy exception. rc G1 c1 Fasting glucose >ULN–160 mg/dL; mild ICI Continue with close follow-up + labs Treatment Initiate insulin for CIADM (or default if diagnosis uncertain) ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.4), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-1 G2 c2 160–250 mg/dL; moderate ICI May hold until glucose control obtained Treatment Insulin (multiple daily injections; long-acting alone insufficient) ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.4), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-1 G3 c3 >250–500 mg/dL (13.9–27.8 mmol/L) ICI Hold until glucose controlled + toxicity ≤G1 Treatment Insulin; early endocrinology consult Acute Assess for DKA ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.4), G3–4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-1 G4 c4 >500 mg/dL (>27.8 mmol/L) or ketoacidosis ICI Hold Acute Admit — DKA management: volume + electrolyte resuscitation, IV insulin, hourly glucose / ketones / pH / anion gap ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.4), G3–4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-1

records.title: Primary adrenal insufficiency
records.subtitle: irAE management · Endocrine
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Adrenal insufficiency s3-adrenal-insufficiency Exclude Secondary (central) AI — low ACTH + low cortisol → manage as hypophysitis. Adrenal CT for metastasis / haemorrhage. Baseline AM ACTH (>2× ULN in primary) + cortisol (<3 µg/dL); ACTH stimulation test if indeterminate (AM cortisol 3–15 µg/dL). Adrenal CT. Red flags Adrenal crisis (hypotension, hyponatraemia) — IV stress-dose hydrocortisone immediately; medical-alert bracelet. rf Rechallenge Hold acutely; resume once stabilised on replacement (endocrinopathy exception). rc G1 c1 Asymptomatic / mild ICI Hold until stabilised on replacement, then resume (endocrinopathy exception) Replacement Hydrocortisone 15–20 mg/day divided (max 30 mg for residual symptoms); add fludrocortisone for mineralocorticoid need ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.2), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-3 G2 c2 Moderate symptoms, ADL intact ICI Hold until stabilised on replacement Replacement Outpatient corticosteroid 2–3× maintenance (hydrocortisone 30–50 mg or prednisone 20 mg/day) for acute symptoms; decrease to maintenance after 2 days ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.2), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-3 G3 c3 Severe symptoms; medically significant ICI Hold Acute IV stress-dose hydrocortisone 50–100 mg Q6–8h; taper to oral maintenance over 5–7 days ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.2), G3–4 G4 c4 Life-threatening (adrenal crisis) ICI Hold; admit Acute IV hydrocortisone stress dose + fluid/electrolyte resuscitation; taper to maintenance ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.2), G3–4

records.title: Thyrotoxicosis / thyroiditis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Endocrine
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Hyperthyroidism s3-hyperthyroidism Thyroiditis s3-thyroiditis Exclude Graves' disease (TSH-receptor Ab; ophthalmopathy/bruit → early endocrine referral) — rare with ICI. Most ICI cases are destructive thyroiditis. Baseline TSH, FT4 (± T3); TSH-receptor Ab if Graves' suspected. Monitor thyroid function every 2–3 wk to catch transition to hypothyroidism (the usual outcome). Red flags Thyroid storm (rare) → hold ICI, inpatient. rf Rechallenge Transient — most transition to hypothyroidism (then treat as such). ICI continued for G1–2. rc G1 c1 Asymptomatic / mild ICI Continue Treatment Beta-blocker (atenolol/propranolol) for symptoms; monitor every 2–3 wk for hypothyroid transition ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.2), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-2 G2 c2 Moderate symptoms, ADL intact ICI Consider holding until symptoms return to baseline (NCCN: may continue if asymptomatic) Treatment Beta-blocker; endocrine consult if Graves' or persistent ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.2), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_ENDO-2 G3 c3 Severe symptoms; medically significant ICI Hold until symptoms resolve to baseline Treatment Beta-blocker + supportive; endocrine ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.2), G3–4 G4 c4 Life-threatening (thyroid storm) ICI Hold; inpatient Treatment Beta-blocker + supportive care; endocrine / consider antithyroid if Graves' ASCO 2021 · Table 4 (4.1.2), G3–4

records.title: Inflammatory arthritis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Rheumatologic
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Arthralgia s13-arthralgia Arthritis s13-arthritis Exclude Osteoarthritis / degenerative joint disease, crystal arthropathy (gout, pseudogout), septic arthritis, soft-tissue rheumatic syndromes (rotator cuff tendinitis); pre-existing crystal / soft-tissue / OA can flare on ICPi. Aspirate to exclude septic joint if infection suspected. Improvement with NSAIDs or steroids (but not opioids) is suggestive of ICPi arthritis. Baseline Full rheumatologic history + exam of all peripheral joints (tenderness, swelling, range of motion) and spine. Inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), ANA, RF, anti-CCP; plain X-ray to exclude metastases / erosions if appropriate; HLA-B27 if reactive-arthritis or axial pattern. NCCN: consider arthrocentesis (cell count, gram stain, culture, crystals), joint ultrasound / MRI if synovitis unclear. Red flags Severe pain with irreversible / erosive joint damage, disabling, limiting self-care ADL -> urgent rheumatology. Early recognition is critical to avoid erosive joint damage; start steroid-sparing agents earlier than in other irAEs given the likely prolonged course. rf Rechallenge G2: hold, resume once controlled. G3-4: hold, may resume in consultation with rheumatology once recovered to <=G1. Consider discontinuing ICPi if arthritis worsens with repeated dosing to where ADL / QoL is severely impaired. Can persist and become a chronic process after ICPi cessation. rc G1 c1 Mild pain with inflammation, erythema, or joint swelling ICI Continue Analgesia Acetaminophen and/or NSAIDs; NCCN: consider intra-articular steroids if only 1-2 joints involved ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.1 IA), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-1 G2 c2 Moderate pain with signs of inflammation, erythema, or joint swelling; limiting instrumental ADL ICI Consider holding Analgesia Escalate analgesia, higher-dose NSAIDs as needed Steroids If inadequately controlled, prednisone 10-20 mg/day; slow taper over 4-6 wk on improvement (if no improvement after 4 wk, treat as G3). If unable to lower below 10 mg/day after 6-8 wk, consider DMARD. NCCN: if unable to taper after 1 wk, increase to 30 mg/day Escalation Intra-articular steroid injections for large joints; DMARD if steroid-dependent. NCCN: csDMARD (methotrexate 15-20 mg weekly + folic acid), IL-6 inhibitor (tocilizumab / sarilumab), or TNF inhibitor Referral Rheumatology ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.1 IA), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-1 G3 c3 Severe pain with signs of inflammation; irreversible joint damage; disabling; limiting self-care ADL ICI Hold temporarily; may resume in consultation with rheumatology if recover to <=G1 Steroids Oral prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day (NCCN: 20-30 mg/day) Escalation If no improvement after 2 wk or worsening -> synthetic or biologic DMARD. Synthetic: methotrexate, leflunomide, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine (alone or in combination). Biologic: anticytokine TNF-alpha or IL-6 antagonist. Caution: IL-6 inhibition can cause intestinal perforation -- do not use with concomitant immune-related colitis Referral Rheumatology ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.1 IA), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-1 G4 c4 Severe / disabling arthritis (ASCO manages G3-4 together; CTCAE Arthritis has no distinct G4) ICI Hold; may resume in consultation with rheumatology once recover to <=G1 Steroids Oral prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day, as per G3 Escalation Synthetic or biologic DMARD as per G3 (methotrexate / leflunomide / hydroxychloroquine / sulfasalazine; TNF-alpha or IL-6 antagonist -- avoid IL-6 with colitis) Referral Rheumatology ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.1 IA), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-1

records.title: Myositis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Rheumatologic
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Myositis s13-myositis Myalgia s13-myalgia Exclude Statin-induced myopathy, polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, muscular dystrophy, generalized fatigue; elevated transaminases may reflect muscle (not liver) -- consider differential with immune-mediated hepatitis. Consider holding statins. CRITICAL: screen for overlap with myocarditis and myasthenia gravis (triple-M / 3M syndrome) -- concomitant myocarditis and/or MG carries high mortality. Baseline CK and aldolase; AST/ALT and LDH may also be elevated; troponin + ECG + echocardiogram or cardiac MRI to evaluate myocardial involvement; anti-AChR + antistriational antibodies for concomitant MG; ESR/CRP; consider EMG, MRI, muscle biopsy, and myositis autoantibodies (anti-TIF1-gamma, anti-NXP2) if diagnosis uncertain; urinalysis for rhabdomyolysis. Monitor: serial CK/aldolase until resolved. Red flags Respiratory muscle weakness, dysphagia, rhabdomyolysis, or concomitant myocarditis / myasthenia gravis (3M overlap) -> hospitalize; high mortality. ASCO: patients with MG-like syndrome or myocarditis and concomitant myositis should be hospitalized. rf Rechallenge Caution with rechallenge -- recurrence on rechallenge reported. Do not restart ICPi until CK is normal and clinical manifestations of myositis have resolved. G2 may require permanent discontinuation if severe objective findings (very elevated enzymes; extensive EMG / MRI / histology involvement). rc G1 c1 Mild weakness with or without pain ICI Continue (NCCN: do not hold if no CK elevation or evidence of active myositis) Steroids If CK and/or aldolase elevated and muscle weakness present, may offer oral prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day Supportive Acetaminophen or NSAIDs for myalgia; consider holding statins ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.2 Myositis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-3 G2 c2 Moderate weakness with or without pain, limiting instrumental ADL ICI Hold temporarily; may resume once CK normal and prednisone <10 mg. Consider permanent discontinuation if severe objective findings Steroids If CK elevated (>=3x ULN), prednisone or equivalent 0.5-1 mg/kg/day (NCCN mild/moderate: prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day) Supportive NSAIDs as needed Referral Early referral to rheumatology or neurology ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.2 Myositis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-3 G3 c3 Severe weakness with or without pain; limiting self-care ADL ICI Hold; consider permanent discontinuation in select patients Steroids Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day; for severe compromise, methylprednisolone IV 1-2 mg/kg or higher-dose bolus (NCCN severe: IV methylprednisolone 500 mg-1 g/day x3 days, then prednisone 1 mg/kg/day) Escalation Plasmapheresis and/or IVIG (note: plasmapheresis immediately after IVIG removes immunoglobulin); biologics (rituximab, TNF-alpha or IL-6 antagonist) if worsening or no improvement after 2 wk; synthetic maintenance (methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate) Work-up + Consider hospitalization for severe weakness limiting mobility, respiratory compromise, dysphagia, or rhabdomyolysis; urgent rheumatology and/or neurology referral ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.2 Myositis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-3 G4 c4 Life-threatening (respiratory muscle or myocardial involvement, rhabdomyolysis); urgent intervention ICI Hold; permanently discontinue Steroids IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg or higher-dose bolus (NCCN: 500 mg-1 g/day x3 days), then prednisone 1 mg/kg/day Escalation Plasmapheresis and/or IVIG (2 g/kg over 2-5 days); rituximab, methotrexate, or mycophenolate. If concomitant myocarditis: cardiology involvement (abatacept with ruxolitinib reported for concomitant myositis + myocarditis) Acute Admit (ICU-level if respiratory / bulbar compromise); cardiology + neurology if 3M overlap ASCO 2021 · Table 5 (5.2 Myositis), G3-4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_MS-3

records.title: Nephritis / acute kidney injury
records.subtitle: irAE management · Renal
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · CTLA-4 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo ctla4 Acute kidney injury s17-acute-kidney-injury Tubulointerstitial nephritis s17-tubulointerstitial-nephritis Creatinine increased s11-creatinine-increased True Exclude Pre-renal (dehydration, volume depletion) and post-renal (obstruction -- image to exclude) causes, acute tubular necrosis, recent IV contrast, nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, PPIs, concomitant chemotherapy), UTI. Most ICPi renal toxicity is acute tubulointerstitial nephritis. Renal allograft recipients are at high risk of rejection -- manage only with transplant-nephrology input. Baseline Serum creatinine before every dose. Urinalysis (sterile pyuria >=5 WBC/hpf supports irAE); BUN, spot urine protein/creatinine + microalbumin/creatinine ratios, urine electrolytes. If new/worsening proteinuria, rule out glomerulonephritis (ANA, ANCA, anti-dsDNA, C3/C4, hepatitis B/C serologies). Renal biopsy not routinely needed -- reserve for steroid-refractory AKI or diagnostic uncertainty; do not delay steroids for biopsy. Red flags Life-threatening / dialysis-requiring AKI, or AKI refractory to steroids -> nephrology, inpatient, escalate immunosuppression. New proteinuria or haematuria -> suspect glomerulonephritis and obtain biopsy. rf Rechallenge G2: resume ICPi only after no recurrence and steroids tapered to <=10 mg/day or discontinued, weighing risks/benefits. G3-4: permanently discontinue ICPi if directly implicated in the renal toxicity. rc G1 c1 Creatinine increase >0.3 mg/dL; 1.5-2.0x above baseline (NCCN Stage 1: 1.5 to =0.3 mg/dL over 48 h) ICI Consider temporarily holding ICPi and/or other contributing agents, pending evaluation of alternative etiologies (IV contrast, medications, fluid status, UTI) and baseline renal function. NCCN: nephrology consult if sustained elevation Steroids Not routinely indicated Monitoring If improved to baseline, resume routine creatinine monitoring ASCO 2021 · Table 6 (6.1 Nephritis/AKI), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_RENAL-1 G2 c2 Creatinine 2-3x above baseline ICI Hold temporarily. If worsening or no improvement after 1 wk -> permanently discontinue. Resume once no recurrence and steroids tapered to <=10 mg/day Steroids If other etiologies ruled out, prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg/day; if worsening / no improvement after 1 wk, increase to 1-2 mg/kg/day. If improved to <=G1, taper over at least 4 wk Escalation NCCN: for persistent stage 2 beyond 1 wk, prednisone / IV methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg/day; consider renal biopsy if no improvement within 5-7 days and/or new proteinuria Referral Nephrology ASCO 2021 · Table 6 (6.2 Nephritis/AKI Follow-Up), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_RENAL-1 G3 c3 Creatinine >3x baseline or >4.0 mg/dL; hospitalization indicated ICI Permanently discontinue if ICPi is directly implicated in renal toxicity Steroids Corticosteroids 1-2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent. If improved to G1, taper over at least 4 wk Escalation If elevations persist >3-5 days or worsen -> additional immunosuppression (infliximab, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide [monthly], cyclosporine, mycophenolate). NCCN: based on biopsy, add azathioprine / infliximab / mycophenolate / rituximab if injury remains >stage 2 after 4-6 wk steroids Work-up + Nephrology consult; hospitalization; monitor creatinine weekly; reflex kidney biopsy discouraged until steroid treatment attempted ASCO 2021 · Table 6 (6.1 Nephritis/AKI), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_RENAL-1 G4 c4 Life-threatening consequences; dialysis indicated; creatinine 6x above baseline ICI Permanently discontinue Steroids Corticosteroids 1-2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent. If improved to G1, taper over at least 4 wk Escalation If elevations persist >2-3 days or worsen -> additional immunosuppression (infliximab, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide [monthly], cyclosporine, mycophenolate) Acute Nephrology; renal replacement therapy / dialysis as indicated; inpatient care ASCO 2021 · Table 6 (6.1/6.2 Nephritis/AKI), G4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_RENAL-1

records.title: Myocarditis
records.subtitle: irAE management · Cardiovascular
records.body: Combo (highest) > PD-1/PD-L1 · CTLA-4 combo pd1 pdl1 ctla4 Myocarditis s1-myocarditis Exclude MI / acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, other cardiotoxic medications, viral or post-vaccination myocarditis; rule out alternative reasons for troponin/CK elevation. Concurrent myositis raises CK/troponin (esp. combination immunotherapy). Baseline ECG (compare to baseline). Troponin (I or T) + CK/CPK + BNP or NT-proBNP. Echocardiogram (with LV strain if possible). Chest X-ray. If troponin elevated, monitor serially. Guided by cardiology: stress test, cardiac catheterisation, cardiac MRI (T1/T2 mapping, modified Lake Louise); consider endomyocardial biopsy / viral titres. Red flags High fatality. Any suspicion -> hold ICI, urgent work-up. Elevated troponin or conduction abnormality -> continuous telemetry + immediate transfer to coronary/intensive care unit; new conduction delay -> consider pacemaker. Watch arrhythmia, heart block, heart failure, cardiogenic shock. Screen the triple-M overlap: myositis + myasthenia gravis + myocarditis. When suspicion is high, treat empirically before confirmatory biopsy. rf Rechallenge Holding ICI is recommended for ALL grades (ASCO). NCCN: discontinue immunotherapy for myocarditis. Do not restart after >=G2 myocarditis; appropriateness of any rechallenge is unknown. rc G1 c1 Abnormal cardiac biomarker testing without symptoms and with no ECG abnormalities ICI Hold for G1 elevated troponin and recheck troponin 6 hours later. May consider resuming once normalised or if believed not to be ICI-related. Work-up + All grades warrant workup and intervention given the potential for cardiac compromise. Steroids High-dose corticosteroids are specified for grade >=2; not indicated at G1 on biomarker abnormality alone. ASCO 2021 · Table 9 (9.1 Myocarditis), G1 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_CARDIO-1 G2 c2 Abnormal cardiac biomarker testing with mild symptoms or new ECG abnormalities without conduction delay ICI Hold and permanently discontinue for >=G2 (ASCO). NCCN: discontinue immunotherapy. Steroids Early (within 24 h) high-dose corticosteroids: prednisone 1-2 mg/kg/day, oral or IV depending on symptoms. NCCN for overt myocarditis: IV methylprednisolone 1 g/day for 3-5 days, then oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day tapered slowly over 6-12 weeks by clinical response + biomarkers. Escalation No immediate response to high-dose steroids -> cardiac transplant-rejection dose methylprednisolone 1 g/day + add mycophenolate, infliximab, or antithymocyte globulin. NCCN: if no improvement in 24-48 h add (alphabetical) abatacept, alemtuzumab, ATG, infliximab (extreme caution if reduced LVEF), IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil (0.5-1 g q12h), or plasmapheresis. Work-up + Admit for cardiology consultation; transfer to coronary care unit if elevated troponin or conduction abnormalities. Referral Cardiology (cardio-oncology preferred). ASCO 2021 · Table 9 (9.1 Myocarditis), G2 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_CARDIO-1 G3 c3 Abnormal cardiac biomarker testing with either moderate symptoms or new conduction delay ICI Hold and permanently discontinue. Steroids Early (within 24 h) high-dose corticosteroids: prednisone 1-2 mg/kg/day (oral or IV). Escalate to methylprednisolone 1 g/day if no immediate response. NCCN: IV methylprednisolone 1 g/day for 3-5 days -> oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, taper 6-12 wk. Escalation No response -> methylprednisolone 1 g/day + mycophenolate, infliximab, or ATG; abatacept or alemtuzumab in life-threatening cases. Infliximab contraindicated at high dose (>5 mg/kg) in moderate-severe heart failure. Work-up + Admit; transfer to coronary/intensive care unit; for new conduction delay consider a pacemaker; manage cardiac symptoms per ACC/AHA guidance with cardiology. Referral Cardiology + ICU-level monitoring. ASCO 2021 · Table 9 (9.1 Myocarditis), G3 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_CARDIO-1 G4 c4 Moderate to severe decompensation, IV medication or intervention required, life-threatening conditions ICI Permanently discontinue. Steroids Cardiac transplant-rejection dose corticosteroids: methylprednisolone 1 g/day IV pulse (ASCO). NCCN: IV methylprednisolone 1 g/day for 3-5 days, then oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day taper over 6-12 weeks once stable. Escalation Add mycophenolate mofetil, infliximab (contraindicated >5 mg/kg in moderate-severe HF; NCCN caution if reduced LVEF), or ATG; consider abatacept or alemtuzumab (+/- ruxolitinib for myositis-myocarditis overlap) as additional immunosuppression in life-threatening cases; IVIG or plasmapheresis (NCCN). Acute ICU/coronary care unit-level monitoring; temporary or permanent pacing as required; manage decompensation per ACC/AHA with cardiology. Referral Cardio-oncology + ICU. ASCO 2021 · Table 9 (9.1 Myocarditis), G4 · NCCN v1.2026 ICI_CARDIO-1

records.title: Pericardial disease
records.subtitle: irAE management · Cardiovascular
records.body: PD-1/PD-L1 · combo pd1 pdl1 combo Pericarditis s1-pericarditis Pericardial effusion s1-pericardial-effusion Exclude MI / acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, malignant pericardial involvement, viral or post-vaccination pericarditis, other cardiotoxic medications. Always consider concurrent myocarditis as a contributor (NCCN). Baseline ECG (compare to baseline). Troponin (I or T) + CK/CPK + BNP or NT-proBNP. Echocardiogram (size the effusion; LV strain if possible). Chest X-ray. Cardiac MRI / catheterisation as guided by cardiology. Evaluate for the triple-M overlap (myositis, myasthenia gravis, myocarditis). Grading ASCO grades cardiovascular irAEs on a biomarker (troponin) ladder, so the grades below describe biomarker-positive / myopericarditis -> high-dose steroids apply. Isolated pericarditis with normal biomarkers: manage per ESC (NSAID + colchicine), not high-dose steroids. Red flags Large or expanding pericardial effusion, hypotension / cardiogenic shock, conduction abnormality -> tamponade is a medical emergency; urgent echocardiogram + immediate cardiology.
